note: Changes to the analysis plan after round2_preregistration.json was written. Each entry records when it was made and what results existed at that time. The pre-registration file itself is never edited.

amendments.results_existing_at_the_time: retrieval run in progress on cell 1 of 9; no answer had been scored by any method
amendments.affects: judge_validation (numeric reference set); no primary metric, test or verdict rule
amendments.change: A question joins the numeric reference set only if its reference answer passes its own numeric check, in addition to the pre-registered conditions (number in the short answer, not a citation). Number parsing also normalises Unicode (NFKC, hyphen and minus variants).
amendments.reason: Measured on the frozen 400 questions before scoring: 298 had a numeric non-citation short answer, but 20 of their reference answers write the number differently (for example 'a few hundredths' for 10^-2, or counts in words), so 'correct' could not be determined for them. 278 remain (counted after the Unicode normalisation in this same change).
amendments.decided_by: Claude, as a correction to a validation step; reported to the user

amendments.results_existing_at_the_time: retrieval run indexing cell 1 of 9; no answer had been generated for the full run or scored by any method
amendments.affects: definition of the primary answer metric nli_fact_recall (priority 1); priority order, tests and verdict rules unchanged
amendments.change: nli_fact_recall counts only the facts that the question's own reference answer entails (NLI, same model). Questions whose reference entails none of its facts have no value for this metric and drop out of its paired comparisons. The pre-registered definition over every fact is kept as the supporting metric nli_fact_recall_all.
amendments.reason: Measured on the frozen 400 questions before scoring: the reference answer entails 716 of its 937 facts (76%), all of them for 219 questions and none for 25. The question writer often added details to the facts that its reference answer does not state, so recall over every fact would score answers on content the reference itself omits. Every cell faces the same facts, so this was noise rather than bias, but it reduced the power to detect a real difference.

amendments.results_existing_at_the_time: retrieval complete; string and NLI scoring complete; Gemma judging just started; no comparison between cells had been run and no verdict computed
amendments.affects: supporting metrics only: nli_faithfulness, nli_context_sufficiency, nli_contradiction. No primary metric, test, threshold or verdict rule changes; nli_fact_recall (priority 1) is unchanged.
amendments.change: These three NLI metrics are reported as measured but unreliable, and no claim in the report rests on them. Faithfulness and context sufficiency are covered instead by the Gemma judge, which scores the same two things per answer.
amendments.reason: Two independent problems. (1) Demonstrated false negatives: for q001, q006 and q007 the answer span was retrieved, the numeric check passed, fact recall was 1.0, and yet every context window was labelled 'neutral', giving faithfulness 0.0. Example q001 answer: 'According to Gartner, 33% of enterprise software applications are projected to embed agentic AI by 2028, up from less than 1% in 2024'. DeBERTa NLI requires the premise to make the hypothesis necessarily true, so a context that states the same fact in different words, or splits the evidence across windows, returns neutral. (2) Mechanical dependence on window count: faithfulness takes the best of N context windows per sentence, so a cell whose context is split into more windows scores higher for that reason alone. Across the 9 cells, Spearman between mean context windows and nli_faithfulness is +0.68, nli_context_sufficiency +0.67, nli_contradiction +0.54. Answer length is nearly constant across cells (83-88 words, 3.6-4.2 sentences), so length does not explain the gap; window count does (fixed_token 4.1-4.4 windows versus grain_growth 2.9-3.4).
amendments.rejected_alternative: Recomputing faithfulness after truncating every context to a common word budget. Context length varies far more within a cell than between cells (grain_growth 74-1956 words, fixed_token 820-1362), so a common budget would discard about a third of fixed_token's context while leaving most grain_growth contexts intact, replacing one bias with another. Redesigning the windowing would mean introducing an untested metric after results existed.
amendments.note_on_fact_recall: nli_fact_recall is computed over windows of the ANSWER, not the context, so context-window count cannot affect it mechanically, and it returned 1.0 on the known-good cases above. It does correlate -0.83 with mean context windows across the 9 cells; that is chunker-mediated (the chunker sets both context length and answer quality) and is reported as a finding with the confound stated, not as a defect.
amendments.decided_by: Claude, as a correction to supporting metrics; reported to the user

amendments.results_existing_at_the_time: retrieval complete; string and NLI scoring complete; Gemma judging 500 of 3600 done; retrieval verdicts computed, answer verdicts not yet (Gemma incomplete)
amendments.affects: supporting metrics only: gemma_faithfulness, gemma_context_sufficiency. No primary metric, test, threshold or verdict rule changes; gemma_correctness (answers, priority 2) is unchanged and validated.
amendments.change: gemma_faithfulness and gemma_context_sufficiency are reported as carrying no information beyond gemma_correctness, and no claim rests on them. With amendment 3 this means round 2 measures neither faithfulness nor context sufficiency independently: the NLI versions are unreliable and the Gemma versions are not separable from correctness.
amendments.reason: Measured on the first 500 judged answers: the three scores are identical for 467 of 500 (93%). Pearson correlations are correctness~faithfulness +0.93, correctness~sufficiency +0.91, faithfulness~sufficiency +0.98. The judge appears to make one overall good/bad decision and apply it to all three dimensions, so the two extra dimensions add no independent signal.
amendments.judge_validation_result: The pre-registered validation of the answer judges passed on the same 500. Against the numeric reference set (n=353), gemma_correctness agrees 92% of the time, averaging 0.98 when the answer contains the right number and 0.21 when it does not. Its distribution is 369 correct, 126 wrong, 5 partial, so it discriminates. nli_fact_recall and gemma_correctness agree substantively (Pearson +0.67; fact recall averages 0.73 when Gemma says correct and 0.02 when Gemma says wrong), which is independent support for the priority-1 answer metric.
amendments.decided_by: Claude, as a correction to supporting metrics; reported to the user

amendments.results_existing_at_the_time: all results complete; verdicts computed and reported
amendments.affects: record-keeping only. No metric, test, threshold or verdict changes, and no code was changed after results existed.
amendments.change: Documents a mismatch between the plan and the implementation of the multiplicity correction. The pre-registration defines the chunker family as '2 comparisons x 3 parsers = 6 tests, Holm'. round2_analysis.py applies Holm within each baseline separately, a family of 3 tests, which is a looser correction than registered.
amendments.reason: Found while explaining the correction to the user after the report was written. Both were computed on the primary retrieval metric and give identical outcomes: grain_growth vs fixed_token is significant on 2 of 3 parsers either way, and grain_growth vs recursive_char on 0 of 3 either way. Under the registered family of 6, the Holm ladder is p=0.0004 vs 0.0083 (pass), p=0.0004 vs 0.0100 (pass), p=0.0222 vs 0.0125 (stop). So the stricter reading that was actually registered supports the same verdicts as the looser one that was run.
amendments.not_done: The code was deliberately not changed. Editing the analysis after results exist is a worse failure than the mismatch itself; the record is corrected instead.
amendments.decided_by: the user, on Claude's recommendation, after Claude found and disclosed the mismatch
